headline: 13 killed, 66 injured in explosion at Qatar gas facility
summary: The blast occurred at the Barzan gas supply facility in Ras Laffan; Bangladeshi nationals are among the injured.
details: At least 13 people were killed and 66 others injured in an explosion at a gas processing facility in Qatar's Ras Laffan industrial city on Sunday evening.
QatarEnergy confirmed that all 13 fatalities were Indian and Pakistani nationals. Bangladeshi nationals are also among the 66 injured, though the exact number has not been immediately known.
The explosion took place at the Barzan gas supply facility. The plant had been suspended since December 2025 for urgent maintenance and was restarted only two days before the incident.
Qatar Energy Minister Saad al-Kaabi stated that the explosion was an accident and not linked to sabotage or any hostile act.
QatarEnergy further noted that the incident posed no environmental risk and did not disrupt the country's export operations.
Ras Laffan is the world's largest LNG export hub, located about 80km north of Doha, and accounts for roughly one-fifth of the global LNG supply.
caption:
13 dead and 66 injured after a massive explosion at one of the world's largest gas hubs in Qatar.

At least 13 people were killed and 66 others injured in an explosion at a gas processing facility in Qatar's Ras Laffan industrial city on Sunday evening.

QatarEnergy confirmed that all 13 fatalities were Indian and Pakistani nationals. Bangladeshi nationals are also among the 66 injured, though the exact number has not been immediately known.

The explosion took place at the Barzan gas supply facility. The plant had been suspended since December 2025 for urgent maintenance and was restarted only two days before the incident.

Qatar Energy Minister Saad al-Kaabi stated that the explosion was an accident and not linked to sabotage or any hostile act.

QatarEnergy further noted that the incident posed no environmental risk and did not disrupt the country's export operations.

Ras Laffan is the world's largest LNG export hub, located about 80km north of Doha, and accounts for roughly one-fifth of the global LNG supply.

headline_marked: 44 floodgates opened as [[Teesta River nears danger mark]], raising flood fears
headline: 44 floodgates opened as Teesta River nears danger mark, raising flood fears
summary: Water levels in Nilphamari have surged, submerging croplands and prompting an orange signal warning for riverbank residents.
details: The Teesta River's water level has surged in Nilphamari, submerging croplands in nearby low-lying areas.
At the Dalia point, the river was flowing just 10cm below the danger level on Monday night, according to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).
To control the situation and prevent further flooding, authorities have opened 44 floodgates of the Teesta Barrage.
An orange signal has been issued at the Dalia point, and local residents in riverbank areas have been alerted to potential risks.
The BWDB warns that water levels may rise further if rainfall continues upstream, increasing the risk for those in char areas.
Residents of Dimla Upazila and other low-lying regions are preparing for potential losses as they monitor the rising waters.
caption:
The Teesta River is rapidly approaching the danger level, forcing authorities to open 44 floodgates to prevent a disaster.

The Teesta River's water level has surged in Nilphamari, submerging croplands in nearby low-lying areas.

At the Dalia point, the river was flowing just 10cm below the danger level on Monday night, according to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).

To control the situation and prevent further flooding, authorities have opened 44 floodgates of the Teesta Barrage.

An orange signal has been issued at the Dalia point, and local residents in riverbank areas have been alerted to potential risks.

The BWDB warns that water levels may rise further if rainfall continues upstream, increasing the risk for those in char areas.

Residents of Dimla Upazila and other low-lying regions are preparing for potential losses as they monitor the rising waters.
